title: Append-only entry invariant, not mechanism
decision: State the append invariant: entries are added at the physical end of their file, never inserted above existing content, and maintain chronological order. The durable rule is the invariant; specific tools (>>, Python append mode) are optional implementation details.
why: Session logs are the audit trail and source of truth. The entire memory system depends on append-only semantics to preserve chronology, prevent accidental rewrites, and guarantee that older entries remain unchanged. Establishing this as a vendor-neutral invariant means any future tooling (shell, Python, editor) must preserve it.
evolution: Future session logging systems and tools must maintain this invariant. Changes to authoring guidance, session-merge logic, or entry-validation rules must not violate append-only ordering.
quote: Use `>>` / Python append mode as the required method for writing session entries.
